slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Decline exclusivity at signing: sign a 12-month nonexclusive pilot (Option N) at $350 a robot, with pre-agreed gates that switch on limited exclusivity (Option M)
The deal is worth less than it is being presented as
–	The $2.0M is a recoupable advance, not extra revenue: three-year OEM cash is $8.7M, not $10.7M
–	Net of all costs, exclusivity is worth +$2.2–2.8M at plan but only −$0.04M to +$0.55M at 65% volumes
The evidence the board requires for irreversible exclusivity does not exist yet
–	Lab uptime is 98.8% against a 99.5% production bar, and the third-party assessment has not started
–	Volumes are unaudited, the growth claim is correlational; the draft lacks audit, floor, release, escrow
The phased N→M structure beats every alternative
–	It earns $50 more a robot, keeps the direct channel and matches X's value even at 24–32% fewer robots
–	It holds cash at least $0.55M above the $2.6M buffer and fails none of the board's conditions
Gates, signposts and next steps make the decision reversible
–	Switch on exclusivity only after certification, two audited quarters of 2,250+ robots and signed protections
–	If the OEM insists on exclusivity at signing, walk away to direct sales plus the integration-firm pilot
–	Start the $0.45M assessment now: it is on the critical path for every OEM route

Key assumptions, and which way each biases the answer
Risks and mitigations: the OEM walking away matters most
▪	$0.9M a year of engineering for all of 2027–29 on every OEM route: conservative, equal across X, N and M; the $0.45M assessment, needed for any OEM production route, is neutral across them
▪	30–70% overlap applied to the $1.8M direct ARR, 2028 cohort only in the base case: favours X (a floor on the lost margin)

▪	The OEM rejects N and M and signs with a competitor (limited leverage): M is the OEM's own proposal; trade price, scope and term; the fallback is direct sales plus the integration pilot
▪	Certification slips past September 2027: start the assessment now; release triggers; no exclusivity until passed
▪	Royalty reporting lag squeezes cash to $0.55M of headroom: monthly remittance, phased engineering, OEM-funded integration work
▪	Support cost, engineering effort or OEM volumes miss the estimate or plan: measure in the pilot and reprice before conversion; Gate 2 uses audited volumes, with a royalty floor after conversion
▪	The competitor claim proves causal after all: gated M still captures exclusivity benefits once proven
